es.text: Mujercitas (Little Women), de Louisa May Alcott, se publicó en dos volúmenes, en 1868 y 1869; en el Reino Unido, la segunda parte apareció por separado como Good Wives. Inspirada libremente en la vida de la autora y de sus tres hermanas, la novela sigue a Meg, Jo, Beth y Amy March en un pueblo de Massachusetts basado en Concord. Mientras su padre sirve como capellán del ejército de la Unión durante la guerra de Secesión, las hermanas crecen guiadas por su madre, Marmee, que lleva la casa y forma el carácter de sus hijas. La vida doméstica, el trabajo y el amor verdadero son los grandes temas del libro. Alcott se retrató a sí misma en Jo, un personaje que ha influido en escritoras posteriores como Margaret Atwood o J. K. Rowling.

en.text: Little Women, by Louisa May Alcott, was published in two volumes, in 1868 and 1869; in the United Kingdom the second part was issued separately as Good Wives. Loosely based on the lives of the author and her three sisters, the novel follows Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy March in a Massachusetts town modelled on Concord. While their father serves as a chaplain in the Union Army during the American Civil War, the sisters grow up guided by their mother, Marmee, who runs the household and shapes her daughters' characters. Domesticity, work and true love are the book's great themes. Alcott portrayed herself in Jo, a character who has influenced later writers such as Margaret Atwood and J. K. Rowling, and the novel has been called the first vision of the “All-American girl”.
